pdf_row.text: Who replaced Sickles | Birney; Hancock | Birney (corps), Hancock overseeing the | sector | Hancock

basis.text: Hancock's report (Official Records 27/1, p. 370): Meade, told that Sickles was wounded, 'directed me to assume command of the Third Corps in addition to that of my own' and the immediate command of the Third passed to Birney. Birney (7 Aug 1863, p. 483), Sickles and Humphreys (sworn, Feb and Mar 1864) and Meade's report (p. 116) put Birney in command of the corps; Hancock and Gibbon (p. 416), and the note of the order of battle, have Hancock put over it. French came later (orders of 7 Jul).

default.label: Birney (corps), Hancock overseeing the sector: Birney commanded the corps, Hancock was placed over it
default.note: The two answers are to two questions: who held the corps (Birney, from about 6 p.m. on 2 July) and who was placed in command above him (Hancock, by Meade's order the same evening, with the Second Corps left to Gibbon). 'Overseeing the sector' is the plan's word for Hancock's command; the sources say 'command of the Third Corps in addition to that of my own'. French, ordered on 7 July, is the later commander.

reason_not_chosen.text: French came to the corps after the battle (orders of 7 July); the conflict asks who took the corps when Sickles fell on 2 July, which was Birney, with Hancock over him.

weighing.summary: The sources do not conflict. Birney, Sickles, Humphreys and Meade say Birney commanded the Third Corps when Sickles fell; Hancock and Gibbon (and the note to the order of battle in the Official Records) say Meade put Hancock in command of the Third Corps in addition to his own; Hancock says in one sentence that the immediate command of the Second passed to Gibbon and that of the Third to Birney. Both are true at different levels: Birney held the corps, Hancock was placed over it. Birney's own report says Hancock reached him about 7.30 with a brigade 'at his request' he assigned a position, which fits Hancock acting as the senior officer on the left and Birney as the corps commander. French, ordered to the corps on 7 July, is the later successor, not a rival: Birney signs as commanding the Third Corps on 7 July and French on 12 July. Settled: every other value is explained by the level of command.
weighing.who: Birney commanded the division that held the left of the corps and took the corps; Sickles was the wounded commander; Humphreys commanded the other division; Hancock was the man Meade placed over the corps; Gibbon took the Second Corps; Meade gave the order; French came on 7 July.
weighing.when: Birney and Gibbon: 7 Aug 1863 (five weeks); Meade: 1 Oct 1863; Hancock's report: before 24 Oct 1863; the Joint Committee testimony of Sickles (26 Feb 1864), Humphreys (21 Mar 1864) and Hancock (22 Mar 1864) is eight months after, under oath; French: 1 Oct 1863. The note of the order of battle was compiled for the Official Records (1889).
weighing.where: Sickles lay wounded near the Trostle house about 6 p.m.; Birney found him there; Humphreys was in his division's line; Hancock was at the Second Corps position and rode to the left; Meade was at his headquarters on the Taneytown road.
weighing.how_knew: Birney acted at Sickles' request; Humphreys received Birney's order; Hancock received Meade's; Gibbon took over the Second Corps from Hancock; Sickles was told by Birney's report and his own handing over; Meade gave the order.
weighing.clock: Not applicable to the point: who held command. Times named in the sources (Birney: 6 o'clock; Hancock to Birney about 7.30) are Union clock readings and are not used to decide between persons.
weighing.independence: Birney's, Sickles', Humphreys', Hancock's, Gibbon's and Meade's statements are six lines of knowledge; Hancock's report and his testimony of 1864 are one line (his own), and Gibbon's relays the order. No source says someone else commanded the Third Corps after Sickles fell.

source_panel_text: Birney held the immediate command of the Third Corps when Sickles fell on Jul 2 (Birney, Sickles, Humphreys and Meade say so); Meade put Hancock over the corps in addition to his own (Hancock, Gibbon). Both are true at different levels. French, ordered on Jul 7, came later. Three other values are listed.

pdf_default.note: 'Birney (corps), Hancock overseeing the sector' holds as the two levels of command; 'overseeing the sector' is the plan's phrase for Meade's order that Hancock take command of the Third Corps in addition to his own.

first_delegated.note: The first pass kept the plan's default with the OR passages; read in context and with the sworn testimony of 1864 it stands. French (later commander, 7 July) is added as a value.

what_would_change_it: Meade's written order of 2 July placing Hancock over the Third Corps (with its hour) or a report that Birney was relieved of the immediate command that evening would change the account; none has been found.
